archetype: A WU generosity-punisher control deck: symmetric table-draw engines (Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Dictate of Kruphix, Temple Bell, Kami of the Crescent Moon) feeding asymmetric hand-size punishers (Iron Maiden, Ebony Owl Netsuke, Viseling), with a checker-passed Aetherflux Reservoir storm kill and a checker-passed Approach of the Second Sun line behind it. deck-audit reads `control` from strategic_frame.json and applies the control overrides, and the frame agrees with the deck. The overrides do not: they ask for 5-7 wipes and 37-39 lands from a deck that kills off a life ledger and an upkeep clock, and they cannot see the punishers at all, because card_roles.json has no entry for Iron Maiden, Ebony Owl Netsuke, Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Dictate of Kruphix or Propaganda. One thing has changed under this reading and it is not the deck: `manabase.pip_requirements` read `card["mana_cost"]`, which Scryfall leaves empty on transform layouts, so the commander's own {2}{W}{W} counted zero white pips. Same 99, measured correctly.
verdict: It functions, it never runs out of cards, and it knows how it wins: turn-three land drops at 0.866, 39 mana sources against a Burgess target of 37, 22 card-advantage copies against a floor of 10, and six checker-passed stacks including a complete table kill. What limits it is white mana at the point of deployment. The deck holds 20 white sources against a target of 36 — short 16, against blue's 5 — and its own commander is {2}{W}{W}. The measured cost is the number to argue with: the probability of two white sources by turn three is 0.41 off lands alone and 0.58 counting rocks, where blue is 0.742 and 0.839. The payoff-timing problem the previous reading named is still real and still second: 75.4% of games have drawn a table-draw engine by turn six and 41.2% have drawn both halves of the pair.

engine.declared: goldfish_targets.json declares six targets: a ten-card symmetric table-draw engine, a six-card asymmetric punisher group, their conjunction, a commander-gated value tax, an eight-card counterspell shell, and win-condition access — with a seventh, THE KILL, resting on one card.

components.reading: The gift. Ten copies, 53.7% of openers, drawn by turn six in 75.4% of games (85.2% ever), mean turn 2.507. The fattest component and the one that arrives first — which is the problem, because on its own it is a donation.

The bill. Six copies, 36.4% of openers, 55.9% by turn six, mean turn 3.045. deck-audit does not flag it — its `thin` flag is size <= 3 and its single-point filter is size <= 1, so a six-card group sits outside both by design. The judgment that six is too few for the component that makes the gift asymmetric is mine, not the audit's.

The conjunction the deck is named after: 41.2% by turn six, 56.7% ever, mean turn 4.215. The pair target's first group is character-identical to the whole engine target, so the pair event is a strict subset and 0.754 − 0.412 = 0.342 is exact — 34.2 points of games reach turn six holding an engine and no punisher. These count cards DRAWN, not cast.

The second, softer tax on the same gift. Seven copies — the corpus's cited 41% of openers — but commander-gated: 54.0% by turn six. The gate is measured by a goldfish that never checks colour, and the commander is {2}{W}{W}.

Eight copies, 67.2% held by turn six, mean turn 2.764. This is the protection budget in fact if not in the taxonomy, and it is healthy — but six of the eight compete with the commit turn for untapped mana. Fierce Guardianship is free while you control a commander and Force of Negation is free off-turn for a blue card, and those two are exactly the ones that survive tapping out.

Win-condition access: 31.2% of openers, 50.5% by turn six — and two of the five are tutors, not kills. It does not name Hullbreaker Horror, without which Aetherflux Reservoir is a four-mana artifact that gains a little life.

THE KILL's own component, and the audit's declared thinnest: one card, 7.1% of an opening seven, and the whole target measures 0.3% by turn six (0.7% ever, 2.4% with tutors). That is the ceiling a one-card component sets, not a simulation defect.

single_points_of_failure.component: The draw punisher group (6 cards — thinnest component of the core two-piece target)
single_points_of_failure.why: It converts a symmetric engine into an asymmetric one. Read the six: only three of them read hand size at all (Iron Maiden, Ebony Owl Netsuke, Viseling); the other three convert draws (Psychosis Crawler, Sphinx's Tutelage, Scrawling Crawler). One further hand-size punisher sits outside the group entirely — Folio of Fancies' {2}{U} mode mills each opponent for their hand size — and the declaration files it with the enablers. The value tax that partially substitutes for it is gated behind the commander, which is gated behind white mana.

lean_into.what: Rebalance the basics: 14 Islands / 3 Plains → 11 / 6. It costs no slot, and it is the largest move available that costs no slot.
lean_into.why: The two colours carry the same effective pip requirement (2) and therefore the same source target (36), because the double-pip cards on each side are Grand Abolisher, Supreme Verdict and the commander in white against nineteen in blue. Blue can afford the loss and white cannot: recomputed through the repo's own manabase functions, moving three basics takes W from 20 sources to 23 and W on-curve from 0.58 to 0.667, while U falls from 31 to 28 and from 0.839 to 0.785 — colour-sources goes -16 to -13 on the worst colour. Do not equalise: five basics would put both colours at roughly 0.72 and 0.74 and blue is the colour with nineteen double-pip cards in it.

lean_into.what: Sequence the punisher before the engine, and mulligan on that axis.
lean_into.why: The deck's asymmetry runs backwards. Duke's rule holds that enablers at least dig toward payoffs, which is why enabler-heavy keeps win — but this deck's enablers dig for all four seats, one card to you and three to the table per cycle. A turn-two Ebony Owl Netsuke does nothing and costs nothing; a turn-two Howling Mine with no punisher is a gift to whoever is fastest. Keep the hand with the punisher and a land.

citations.quote: Payoffs without the enabler are blanks until the engine exists; enablers without payoffs at least dig toward them — an asymmetry that usually favors keeping the enabler-heavy hand.
Every single-target card you cast is a net loss against the table: you spend a card, one opponent loses a card, and two bystanders profit from the exchange for free.

cut_candidates.why: A land that produces no coloured mana in a deck sixteen white sources short of target. Three lands in the 99 produce no colour — Ancient Tomb, Flooded Strand and Mikokoro — and of those, Ancient Tomb makes two mana and Flooded Strand fetches Plains-or-Island (so it is colour fixing in fact, even though land_colors reads it as nothing). Mikokoro is the one whose only contribution is an ability the deck already owns ten copies of. Replacing it with a white-producing land buys a white source at zero cost to the land count.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: This is real, and it is the cut I expect to be argued with. Mikokoro is a repeatable each-player-draws-one at instant speed from a land slot: it is on-plan, it is a punisher trigger every turn once Iron Maiden or Ebony Owl Netsuke is down, and it survives artifact and enchantment removal in a way that Howling Mine and Font of Mythos do not. It also comes out of the land slot rather than a spell slot, so cutting it is the one cut here that does not buy a spell back. I am recommending it because the games it wins are games where the deck already has its colours, and the games white mana loses are the ones it never gets to.

cut_candidates.why: Six mana to give an opponent seven cards every time they cast a spell. The deck's own strategic_frame names it as a trap in two of its four matchup frames — the aggro frame ('Forced Fruition refuels their hand') and the combo frame ('hands a storm pilot seven cards per spell'). Opponents discard to seven at cleanup, so the payoff stack 003 verifies is 3 from Iron Maiden plus 4 from Ebony Owl Netsuke on that opponent's upkeep — seven cards paid for seven damage, and only when both punishers are already down, which is 41.2% by turn six.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: No other card in the 99 puts seven cards into an opponent's hand from one trigger, repeatedly, at no mana cost to you: Font of Mythos gives two per draw step, Howling Mine (only while untapped), Dictate of Kruphix and Kami of the Crescent Moon one each, Temple Bell and Kwain and Loran one per activation, Jace Beleren one per +2, The Second Doctor one per end step, and Prosperity, Skyscribing, Braingeyser, Stroke of Genius and Mathemagics each do it once for real mana. Stack 003 — one of six checker-passed artifacts and the only one that proves the punisher clock — is built on a board containing it. Cutting it drops the table-draw component from ten copies to nine. A reasonable pilot keeps it and holds it until both punishers are down; I recommend the cut because the card is most dangerous in exactly the games where they have not arrived.

add_candidates.why: The same gift, given on your clock instead of theirs. Forced Fruition pays out whenever an opponent chooses to cast a spell; Windfall pays out when you cast it, for three mana instead of six, so it can be held until Iron Maiden and Ebony Owl Netsuke are on the battlefield and fired in your second main before their upkeeps. The cost cuts against the deck's hoarding posture: Windfall discards your own hand including held counterspells, and the deck runs three separate 'no maximum hand size' effects precisely so it can hoard. A pilot who would rather not throw away a held Fierce Guardianship should spend this slot on Black Vise.

gaps: This diagnosis exists because `manabase.pip_requirements` read `card["mana_cost"]`, which Scryfall leaves empty on transform and MDFC layouts, so every double-faced spell counted zero coloured pips — including this deck's own {2}{W}{W} commander. The decklist has not changed (sha 2d7f07f9… still matches cards.json); only the measurement did. The previous diagnosis's colour-sources reading quoted 'W at 20 against 22': the 20 was right and the 22 is now 36. Its verdict for the axis was already 'weakness'; the direction was right and the size was not.

The Karsten target of 36 is the repo's own hypergeometric at turn three on the play over 99 cards, not Karsten's published figure. His table gives 33 sources for a {C}{C} spell (Grand Abolisher), 29 for 1{C}{C} (Supreme Verdict) and 26 for 2{C}{C} (the commander). The deck's 20 is under all three, so the finding does not depend on which number you prefer — but a reader who wants the smallest honest gap should use 26 and read it as short six for the commander, not short sixteen.

W's effective_pips is 2 by exactly the quorum and no margin: PIP_WEIGHT_QUORUM is 0.20, 15 cards carry a white pip, ceil(15 × 0.20) = 3, and exactly three cards want {W}{W}. Cut Grand Abolisher or Supreme Verdict and white's effective requirement falls to one pip, its target falls from 36 to 22, and the axis reads short two instead of short sixteen. That is a genuine sensitivity in the measure and the pilot should know it before spending four slots. It is not a reason to dismiss the finding — the commander is one of the three and cannot be cut, so the requirement cannot be legislated below {W}{W}.

Every figure I give for the proposed mana package is RECOMPUTED by me through manabase's functions on a hypothetical 99, not read from a tracked artifact. It is ◆ by construction and reproducible, but it is not mana_analysis.json. The first open question exists to replace it with a measurement.

No deck_recon.json exists for this deck (deck-audit freshness reports recon.present false) and no log_annotations.json exists — no games are logged on any deck. Nothing here is weighed against what strong Heliod, the Radiant Dawn lists actually run or against anything that happened at a table. The Forced Fruition and Mikokoro cuts in particular are argued from this deck's artifacts and the corpus alone.

card_roles.json classifies 85.9% of this deck and the twelve unclassified cards are not incidental — Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Dictate of Kruphix, Iron Maiden, Ebony Owl Netsuke and Propaganda are the deck's identity. Every axis count is a floor and I have said so where it changes the reading.

The sweepers axis carries a target of 5-7 from the control archetype override while quoting a source that says one or two max. The corpus cannot settle which applies to a deck that never needs the board clear; I called it adequate on the quote rather than the override, and a reader may reasonably disagree.

bracket_report.json carries no decklist_sha256, so deck-audit could not confirm it describes the current 99. Every bracket_delta above was recomputed directly through bracket.assess rather than read from it; base floor 4, and all seven paired swaps land on 4.

Counting Mystic Gate as a full white source is optimistic — it filters rather than produces, so it is a second white source and never a first. The package's measured movement includes it at full weight; discount roughly one source if you reject that convention.
